source.title: Ulster Herald, 21 May 1949, p. 5 ("Four contests in Omagh rural election")
source.publisher: Ulster Herald (via the Irish Newspaper Archives)
source.check: Original citation restored 6 Nov 2026 (the 5 Nov verification had moved it because of a text-cleaning fault).

note: Triennial election of the electoral divisions of Omagh rural district, one member each, polled on 2 June 1949. For the first time in 25 years four divisions were contested (Bencran, Gortin, Maine, Moyle), three by Anti-Partitionists and one by an Independent, all against Unionists. 'Seventeen Unionists and seventeen Anti-Partitionists were returned unopposed, but in one Nationalist division no nomination was received and the retiring member will be deemed re-elected'; four new members came in unopposed (Ulster Herald, 21 May 1949, p. 5). The unopposed members are recorded from the Returning Officer's Notice of Result (Ulster Herald, 11 June 1949, p. 2), read from the page OCR. Tattymoyle has no candidate in the notice's name columns; its column 6 names the retiring councillor, Peter Connolly, as re-elected (read on the block image, 7 Nov 2026). New member. Returned unopposed.
correctionNote: Renamed from 'Moorefield' to Moorfield (19 Nov 2026, w19-tidy, the owner's decision 4 of 19 Nov 2026: a division filed under two spellings takes its official name, and each round keeps the spelling it was filed under as Constituency_Name_As_Printed): the Northern Ireland DED maps of 1921-69 name the DED Moorfield; the rounds were filed as Moorfield (1930, 1933, 1946, 1952, 1955, 1958, 1961, 1964, 1967); Moorefield (1949). This round was filed as 'Moorefield', kept as Constituency_Name_As_Printed; the old address (moorefield) answers with a redirect to this one.
